reserve.h1: One network across the whole reserve.
reserve.study_area: the study area around the lodges
reserve.stat4_label: clear carrier uplink into the reserve
reserve.s02_lede: Carrier connectivity comes into the reserve once. Everything past that point runs on infrastructure the reserve owns.
reserve.layer1_tail: LTE failover keeps the reserve connected if the carrier path drops.
reserve.layer3_p: Sector radios reach the lodges, HQ, the anti-poaching base, ecology, the workshop and the gates. A LoRaWAN gateway is ready for fence, water-point, pump and fuel sensors.
reserve.next_p: Once the backbone covers the reserve, a new camera, sensor or lodge is an endpoint on a network that is already there. It is not a new infrastructure project or a new provider contract.
reserve.prof_caption: 5.8 GHz · k = 4/3 · uplink tower 30 m · high-site masts 18 m · lodge masts 8 m. Lodge positions come from published GPS coordinates.
reserve.s04_lede: A reserve network carries three loads at once. This design is built to hold all three on one backbone.
reserve.s06_lede: A reserve that replaces a separate rented connection and rented Wi-Fi at every lodge with one owned backbone typically recovers the investment in under three years on connectivity costs alone. The security, operations and guest-experience benefits come on top of that.
reserve.s06_hook: Send us each lodge's latest connectivity invoice, or just the monthly totals, and we will work out {SHORT}'s actual payback. It takes us a day.
reserve.s06_forward: If infrastructure decisions sit with someone else, please pass this on. Owners will find the payback and ownership case, the reserve manager the security and operations case, and lodge managers the guest experience case.
reserve.s07_title: What changes when the reserve owns it
with_list: One uncontended carrier feed shared across the reserve
Lodges, HQ, the anti-poaching base and gates on one private network
Coverage out into the field, day and night
An owned asset that takes cameras and sensors without new towers
reserve.lens_eff: Water points, pumps and fuel tanks report their own status, so there are fewer vehicle trips just to check. Maintenance, ecology and lodges share one communications path.
reserve.lens_own: High sites, backbone and power belong to the reserve. The network grows with the reserve instead of depending on each lodge's separate provider.
reserve.lens_exec: Management gets live visibility of the network, cameras and sensors, and a record of operational diligence for owners, insurers and conservation partners.
reserve.step1: Your lodges' current connectivity costs, your peak usage, the incidents that were hardest to coordinate, and what currently needs a vehicle trip to check.
reserve.step2: A marked map of HQ, the anti-poaching base and the gates. We add them to the model and rerun the link plan.
reserve.step3: We walk the high sites and relay points, and confirm the carrier uplink with Vodacom.

wind.h1: A second path for SCADA, crews and cameras.
wind.study_area: the study area around the turbines
wind.stat4_label: clear carrier uplink into the site
wind.s02_lede: The fibre stays the primary path. An owned wireless path runs alongside it and takes over automatically when the fibre is cut or stolen.
wind.layer1_tail: It gives the site an independent route out when the fibre route is down.
wind.layer3_p: Sector radios reach the substation, the O&M building and the turbine strings, so SCADA, crew radios and perimeter cameras keep reporting on the standby path.
wind.next_p: Once the standby backbone covers the site, extra cameras, met-mast data or crew devices are endpoints on a network that is already there, not a new project.
wind.prof_caption: 5.8 GHz · k = 4/3 · uplink tower 30 m · high-site masts 18 m · site masts 8 m. Turbine and substation positions come from OpenStreetMap.
wind.s04_lede: A wind farm network carries three loads at once. The standby path is designed to hold all three when the fibre is down.
wind.s06_lede: On a wind farm the case is not a lower bill. It is keeping SCADA visible, crews reachable and cameras reporting when the fibre is cut or stolen. A standby wireless path costs far less than a day of lost visibility.
wind.s06_hook: Tell us how often the fibre has been cut in the last two years and how long SCADA was blind each time, and we will size the standby path for {SHORT} to match.
wind.s06_forward: If this decision sits with someone else, please pass it on. The asset manager will find the availability case, the site manager the crew and O&M case, and security the camera case.
wind.s07_title: What changes with an owned standby path
with_list: SCADA keeps reporting when the fibre is cut
Crews reachable across the site on one network
Perimeter cameras stay online during an incident
An owned asset the site controls, monitored remotely
wind.lens_eff: Crews keep working across the site when the fibre is down, and faults are seen remotely before a vehicle is sent.
wind.lens_own: The standby masts, radios and power belong to the site. They are monitored remotely and independent of the fibre route.
wind.lens_exec: The asset manager gets a documented second path for SCADA and a record of operational diligence for lenders, insurers and the grid operator.
wind.step1: How often the fibre has been cut, how long SCADA was blind, and where crews lose contact on site.
wind.step2: The O&M building, the substation and the fibre route on a marked map. We add them to the model and rerun the link plan.
wind.step3: We walk the high sites, confirm the uplink with Vodacom and check mounting at the substation.
